title: UK Hits Hottest Day of the Year at 38.1°C!
summary:
Imagine stepping outside and feeling like you're in an oven. That's what it was like in the UK on Thursday, August 13, 2026, when temperatures hit 38.1 degrees Celsius (100.6 degrees Fahrenheit) in west London. That's the hottest day of the year so far!

This is the UK's fifth heat wave of the year, and the first one was way back in May. 2026 has now had a record four days with temperatures of 36°C or higher. France is even hotter, with some places nearing 41°C (106°F).

The heat is causing big problems. In Britain, nurses have collapsed from heat exhaustion while working in hospitals. Many hospital buildings are old and don't have good cooling. Nicola Ranger from the Royal College of Nursing said, "When nursing staff are collapsing... it shows just how badly they are being failed."

There's also a serious drought. Rivers are drying up, and crops are shriveling. Southern Water in England has asked for a rare drought order to ban businesses from using water for things like washing cars. If approved, it would be the first such ban since May 2006.

Wildfires are a huge danger. In northern Greece, over 300 people were evacuated by sea from a resort after a wildfire. In England, firefighters are battling a blaze in the New Forest. So far this year, 1,017 wildfires have been recorded in England and Wales—the same as last year's record.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he might ban disposable barbecues because of the fire risk. "People should not be using those barbecues outside at this moment in time," he said. With no rain in sight, everyone is hoping for a break from the heat.
why_it_matters: Extreme heat can affect whether you can play outside, how cool your school or home stays, and how much water your family is allowed to use.

WHAT: The UK recorded its hottest day of the year at 38.1°C in west London, with record heat, drought, and wildfires.
WHERE: West London and other UK areas, with even hotter weather in France and dangerous fires in northern Greece.
WHY: Extreme heat caused health problems, water shortages, and fire risks, with no rain in sight.
